title: X Feed Digest
summary: Google shipped a major Gemini 3 Deep Think upgrade while OpenAI published a GPT‑5.2 physics preprint—labs are emphasizing research‑grade reasoning and scientific impact.
Agent/coding tooling advanced: Anthropic released a Skills‑for‑Claude playbook, Claude Code’s Bash tool got ~7× faster, and gogcli v0.10.0 added deeper Docs/Slides support.
Benchmarks and workflows are maturing—SWE‑rebench now shows Opus 4.6 and Codex 5.3 leading, and real‑world NotebookLM grading workflows surfaced.
Markets chatter was light but included an upcoming earnings-heavy week and on‑chain buzz around a 10k BTC transfer; a viral thread debated a Dutch unrealized‑gains tax proposal.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Gemini 3 Deep Think upgrade
items.body: Google rolled out a major upgrade to Gemini 3’s Deep Think reasoning mode, positioning it for practical engineering and research tasks. The demo highlights sketch‑to‑3D workflows that generate printable files from drawings.

items.title: @OpenAI: GPT‑5.2 physics preprint
items.body: OpenAI announced a theoretical physics preprint where GPT‑5.2 helped derive a new result on gluon interactions. The work claims a previously‑assumed zero‑amplitude interaction can occur under specific alignment conditions.

items.title: @aiwithmayank: Skills playbook for Claude
items.body: Anthropic released a 30+ page guide on designing reusable “Skills” for Claude, shifting focus from prompt tweaks to structured execution layers. The guide emphasizes progressive disclosure, testing, and workflow patterns for reliable agents.

items.title: @jarredsumner: Claude Code Bash speedup
items.body: Claude Code’s Bash tool is getting a big performance boost in the next version. The author reports a 7× speedup and lower memory use when streaming large stdout workloads.

items.title: @steipete: gogcli v0.10.0
items.body: gogcli shipped a major release with deeper Docs/Slides support (markdown tables, tab‑aware editing, template slides) plus Drive and Gmail improvements. It’s a notable upgrade for Google‑Workspace automation from the terminal.

items.title: @andrew_n_carr: SWE‑rebench results
items.body: SWE‑rebench published its Jan–Feb results: Opus 4.6 and Codex 5.3 top the chart at ~51.7% resolve rate. The update also highlights strong showings from newer Chinese models like Qwen.

items.title: @ihtesham2005: NotebookLM grading workflow
items.body: A viral story described a professor using NotebookLM to grade essays at scale with rubrics, style‑shift checks, and personalized feedback. It’s a compelling example of AI workflows reducing grading time while improving response quality.

items.title: @Stocktwits: Earnings calendar
items.body: A heavy earnings week is coming up, with names like PANW, CDNS, WMT, BABA, ETSY, DE, and BKNG on deck. Useful quick scan for anyone planning trades or news monitoring.

items.title: @Tradewith_kd: 10k BTC transfer
items.body: On‑chain chatter highlighted a 10,000 BTC transfer from an early‑era wallet—about a $1B move at today’s prices. The event underscores how early holdings still swing sentiment when they move.

items.title: @XFreeze: Dutch unrealized‑gains tax thread
items.body: A viral thread claimed the Netherlands approved a 36% tax on unrealized gains, sparking debate about forced selling and market impact. Treat as a discussion thread, not a verified policy summary.

items.title: @om_patel5: App Store approval checklist
items.body: A concise checklist for avoiding App Store rejections—privacy policy, account deletion, test credentials, clear pricing, and no “coming soon” features. A good pre‑submit sanity pass for indie devs.

items.title: @_FORAB: X to crack down on spam accounts
items.body: X’s product lead reportedly said the platform will step up enforcement against AI/spam accounts, including bans on associated accounts. The announcement sparked debate in replies about creator payouts and spam signals.

items.title: @shiri_shh: Local‑biz site automation idea
items.body: A founder pitched an OpenClaw‑powered workflow to scrape local business data, auto‑generate websites, and sell activation via email. It’s a simple SMB lead‑gen idea with a numbers‑driven revenue model.
